info.name: Nexmile — Customer app
info.description:
Everything the **customer app** needs. Rider and merchant endpoints live in their own collections.

**Order to run:** Authentication → Addresses → Restaurants → Cart → Checkout. The OTP verify request stores the tokens, and later requests capture restaurant, cart-line and order ids as they go, so the whole flow runs top to bottom without editing anything.

**Money is a JSON number** and loses its zero fraction: ₹430.00 arrives as `430`. Read it as `num`, never `double`.

**Refresh must be serialised behind one lock.** Two concurrent refreshes with the same token are treated as a stolen token and sign the user out everywhere.

Full walkthrough: `docs/CUSTOMER_APP_FLOW.md`

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: No separate registration endpoint — the account is created on first successful verification. Email OTP today; when SMS clears DLT you send `phone` instead of `email` on the same endpoint.

request.description: Send `email` **or** `phone`, never both. `intended_role` only matters when the account does not exist yet — an existing user keeps the role they have.
Returns the user plus an access/refresh pair, and stores both in collection variables. A customer comes back `active` immediately — no waiting.
Call once on a 401, then retry the original request. **One at a time** — parallel refreshes are treated as a stolen token.
The signed-in user, their role and status.
Every device holding a live refresh token.
Sign one device out.
Ends this session only.
Ends every session on every device.
Name, phone, email, preferred language.
New accounts are named "Nexmile user" until this is called — prompt for a real name on first run. `preferred_locale` is `en`, `ta` or `hi`.
Irreversible.

item.name: 3. Delivery addresses
item.description: **latitude and longitude are required.** Delivery is capped at 1 km and matching is done on coordinates — an address without a pin cannot be matched to any restaurant.

request.description: Newest first. The default one is flagged.
`label` is `home`, `work` or `other`. Prefill coordinates from GPS and let the user drag a pin.

body.raw:
{
    "label": "home",
    "contact_name": "Meena",
    "contact_phone": "9876543210",
    "line1": "12 Anna Salai",
    "line2": null,
    "landmark": "Opposite the bus stand",
    "city": "Madurai",
    "pincode": "625001",
    "latitude": 9.9252,
    "longitude": 78.1198
}

request.description: A single address.
Send only the fields being changed.
The one checkout preselects.
Past orders keep their own copy of the address.

item.name: 4. Restaurants
item.description: Ranked open first, then nearest. Closed shops are listed below open ones rather than hidden — an empty screen at 3pm reads as "Nexmile does not work here".

request.description: Gate the UI on `is_open`. `is_accepting_orders` and `within_operating_hours` say **why** it is shut — "closed until 6pm" and "not taking orders" are different messages.
Same endpoint using raw device coordinates.

Surplus food at a discount, soonest to expire first. Only deals orderable **right now** appear, so the screen never advertises something checkout would refuse. Show the countdown and `portions_left` — a rescue deal is a race.
Storefront plus the weekly opening hours.

`data.menu` is categories with items; items with no category come back separately under **`uncategorised`** — render both, or a shop that never made categories looks empty.

Out-of-stock items are returned, not hidden. Show them struck through.

item.name: 5. Cart
item.description: One cart per restaurant, and they persist. Glancing at another shop does not empty the basket you started. Every response comes back fully priced — never compute a total in the app.

request.description:
Required choices are enforced **here**, not at checkout — a 422 on `option_ids` means open the customisation sheet.

Identical lines merge; different options stay separate.

query.description: delivery | pickup — pickup previews the price with no delivery fee

request.description:
Gate the checkout button on **`can_checkout`** — it already accounts for the minimum, sold-out items, an empty cart and the restaurant being closed.

`unavailable_items` names dishes that sold out while the cart sat there. Leave them in place and show them struck through; a basket that quietly shrinks is worse than one that explains itself.
`quantity: 0` removes the line, so the minus button needs no special case at the boundary.
Remove one line.
Clear everything.
Every restaurant with an unfinished basket — reads a "you have an unfinished order" banner.

item.name: 6. Checkout and orders
item.description: Cash on delivery only for now. A COD order is created at `placed` and reaches the restaurant immediately.

request.description:
Everything is re-checked here — availability, opening hours, the 1 km radius, the minimum. Expect 422s even when the cart looked fine, and show `errors.<field>[0]` verbatim:

- `cart` — empty, below the minimum, or an item sold out
- `merchant` — closed or not taking orders
- `address_id` — outside the radius, or no pin
- `payment_method` — not available yet

The cart is emptied on success, so tapping back cannot place it twice.
No address needed and no delivery fee charged.

Small and cheap — poll every few seconds while in flight. Returns the status, the estimate, the pickup code, and the rider's name, phone and **live position** while they are carrying it.

`cancellation_reason` is written by the merchant for the customer — show it verbatim.

query.description: in-flight only, for a home-screen banner

request.description: Newest first. Each order keeps its own snapshotted prices and item names.
Full order with items, options and the status timeline.
Returns a **printable HTML page**, not JSON — open it in a webview or the system browser.
Only while the status is `placed`. Once the restaurant accepts, this returns 422 — hide the button as soon as the status moves on.
